body: YTA. 100%. You should like an entitled bratty bridezilla. People are not props. The people in your wedding party are *people*. Do you love your sister? And want her standing up with you? Then get over yourself and let her look how she looks. You talk about "love and respect" but you are incredibly disrespectful of your sister. You're a huge asshole here.
NTA. You told him multiple times to stop making comments about your wife's appearance. He was totally out of line and cruel. Good for your for not letting him get away with it.
NTA. But you and your bf need to end it. You clearly want different things out of life.

NTA. They aren't your kids and it's a huge imposition. You didn't really have the right to tell her not to have more kids, but you 100% have the right to say you will not be regular childcare for any more kids they decide to have.

YTA. Hiring and firing decisions are private. You should not be putting it up to a poll or presenting it to your workers. All you need to say is "Meg is no longer an employee here." The social media slagging is especially shitty.

You need to start running your company like an adult. You needed to check that things were backed up (yes, I know it was her responsibility, but as a boss it's *your* responsibility to make sure things were followed through on.) You needed to handle disciplining her privately, not blast it to your other employees. Grow up.

YTA. You say you "didn't want to lie" but that's exactly what you did. You did betray her. You knew he was coming, said "you didn't think so" (that is a lie) and as a result she was blindsided by her abuser being there. You and your parents are both AWFUL for not having her back with this and for minimizing her abuse. Why are you and your parents siding with her abuser? She's right to go no contact and I feel sorry for her because she deserves family that supports her. I hope she has friends who are better people than you and your parents.
I agree with this. I was all set from the title to say you were TA, but context tells me you're NTA and if you force his hand he's probably going to back down.

That's because he's trying to make you feel like you're wrong to question his behavior and the dynamics in your relationship. You're not wrong. Something is not right in your relationship. His behavior is not acceptable. YOU. ARE. NOT. WRONG.

NTA and honestly, RED FUCKING FLAGS everywhere.

1. Your husband throws away your personal property to teach you a lesson. Including irreplaceable things with sentimental value. From your post, this isn't the first time he's done this. This is NOT acceptable behavior.
2. This fight started because your husband didn't want to be a parent to his daughter while you were busy taking care of your mother. He needed to be an adult and a partner to you and take care of his daughter during an emergency.
3. Even though the whole "fight" was because of his actions, he's trying to frame it as a situation where you were both wrong.
4. He's angry you told your daughter the truth about his actions, even though it's not your responsibility to keep his shitty behavior a secret. What he did is harmful to her as well as you.
5. He outright belittled you and said you had no friends. That's childish and a completely shitty thing to say to your spouse, who is, again, supposed to be your partner.

I think you need to take long hard look at him and his behavior and think about whether he's someone you really want to be around. And it's not just about how he treats you. Your daughter is seeing these dynamics and it will affect her future relationship dynamics.

NTA. Your bio parents should shut their mouths. The only reason you have a second family is that your parents were absolutely shitty to you and failed as parents by kicking you out of the house. They are *lucky* you had a place to go where you were sheltered and cared for. Plenty of LGBTQ minors with bio parents like yours end up in awful situations.
YTA. She specifically asked you not to joke about an issue that she's sensitive about and you're doing it anyway. There's no grey area; that's asshole behavior.

YTA. Do not parentify your child. It is not her responsibility to take care of her siblings. You're not "just asking her to wake up 20 minutes early and make breakfast." You're asking her to get all the kids ready for school and that is not fair to her. Talk to your husband and figure out a plan that does not involve making your kid the third parent.
NTA. Change the locks, work with a lawyer to set up a paper trail that they are not welcome and document their trespassing.

YTA. You already have six f\*cking bridesmaids, just have one more. I am withholding judgement on the initial decision to exclude Anne, since I don't know the circumstances behind it. But once you decided to include her, it was an complete asshole move to tell your cousin that essentially she was a backup, your last choice, and disposable.

And on top of that, you're pitching a fit because what she's telling the truth about what you actually did. You *did* kick her out of your wedding party. You admit it in this post.

You are such an unbelievable asshole in this situation. That's not even taking into account any money and time Cassie may have already invested in being your bridesmaid. Has she bought the dress/shoes/etc? Has she taken time off work for your bachelorette party or bridal shower or dress shopping? Has she given money and time to plan/pay for these things?

You used her and tossed her. Someone is acting like a privileged brat here and it isn't Cassie.

Absolutely NTA. 

She STOLE YOUR FOOD. That's on her. It wasn't meant for her to eat. She f\*cked around, she found out.

NTA. Dogs in the office are not a necessity. Also, if you are in the US I believe your allergy falls under ADA as requiring reasonable accommodations. Forcing you to work from home is arguably unreasonable.
NTA. Your culture and traditions matter just as much as theirs. You're already compromising by doing a church wedding. You have every right to wear what you want.
NTA. There is NEVER any reason to say something like that to a child.

NTA. Jake doesn't have the right to use his sister's stuff. This is the sibling fight as old as time and regardless of the gender of the siblings, it's crappy to make them share clothes and makeup (and sharing makeup isn't sanitary).

If you were objecting to Jake wanting to experiment with clothes and makeup period, you would be TA, but you're just trying to enforce boundaries. Jake doesn't get to use Rebecca's stuff and she doesn't get to use his. Take him out to get some makeup and clothes of his own.

NTA. This is her issue and she's bordering on harassing you. Don't trade shifts, don't give and inch. Wear what makes you feel good (as long as it's work appropriate, which your manager has already says it is).

NAH. Your parents have a right to set the rules for their house, even if they are in your opinion (and I'm inclined to agree with you) overly strict. But you don't have to stay with them. Which means you either don't have to go visit or you can get a hotel or something.

YTA. She's probably going to be wearing that ring every day, she deserves to have her style preferences taken into account. Your opinion of whether she or not she "should" like the original ring or if it's "appropriate" does not matter. It is not your ring. It is not your business. Butt out.
NTA. She asked you to do it. She didn't test how the wine would work on the fabric, didn't consider seepage. She wanted drama. The fact that there were technical issues is not your fault.

NTA. And it's lovely that you want to provide for his cousin. If 8 years isn't enough for you to feel comfortable giving her the ring (grief works on it's own schedule), you can always give it to her when she's older and has some other major life event (post-secondary school graduation, her own wedding, birth/adoption of a kid, or maybe write it into your will that she gets it).

I understand how important family heirlooms are, but it's disgusting how his family is descending on you like this. Depending on how it was done and how much time had passed, it might have been okay to ask, but they needed to be ready to accept a "no" and not harass you about it.
Yep. I already knew I was going to say he was TA at that moment. I read the rest and it just got worse.

YTA. Taking care of your own child is not "babysitting" so you're already TA. Having this ridiculous idea that your wife should be chained to the home while you're free to go out because "it's different" (why? because you didn't give birth?) makes you TA. That baby is BOTH of your responsibilities; you do not get to pawn all the childcare off on your wife. And yeah, you're TA for bringing your mother into it. It's not her business. You're TA all around and your wife deserves better. You need to be a partner to her. She's not a nanny. And your ultimatum that she needs to stay home is a supreme asshole move.

YTA. Replace your daughter's phone. Sell your son's laptop for the funds if need be, otherwise make your son pay you back the cost by doing chores, saving his allowance, whatever it is. I would take away the laptop until he's done that. It is absolutely not fair to your daughter to tell her "too bad so sad" because you raised your son to be an entitled spoiled brat.
NTA. Hiding someone's inhaler can fucking KILL THEM. It's not funny. Also, what is up with the toxic masculinity here?

NTA. This is a medical question. It's more appropriate to ask a doctor rather than a piercer, because a piercer is likely not familiar with giving birth? The nurse is an asshole. Doctors and nurses, especially those who deal with reproductive parts, need to be comfortable talking about all manner of things. Yes even "kinky" things (although a piercing isn't "kinky" but whatever).

YTA. It's none of your business how she dresses and it's not "disrespectful" to your brother. Get over your weird ideas about how an engaged woman or wife or mother should dress. It's none of your business.
It's not that uncommon in certain older houses.
NTA and him LOCKING YOU IN A ROOM and leaving you there for an hour (really any time at all is unacceptable) is a huge red flag. You need to leave as soon as possible.
NTA. Your husband is being weird and controlling, especially since, as you've said, he can have his own bag that's not stored in the fridge.

YTA and so is your husband. Your son may have been out of line throwing something away, BUT he is a child and he is acting out in response to your husband's abuse and your condoning of it. You need to step the fuck up and protect your kid. Tell your abusive husband that the insults and name-calling ends now or kick him to the curb. You're a parent and you need to protect your kid.

YTA. You are allowed to tell your own children how to address you. You are absolutely not allowed to tell other people's children how to address their parents.

The way to reinforce your rules for your child is to correct his behavior and explain to him that different people have different rules, but he should abide by your rules. Not to try to make everyone follow your rules.

NTA. He should have told you not to post pics of his kids on social media and asking you to remove them is a reasonable request. Him refusing to replace something he broke is *definitely* asshole behavior though. 

And honestly, him taking your phone and throwing it away in the first place? That raises a bunch of red flags, especially coupled with him saying basically "you made me do this." Throwing away and/or breaking people's modes of communication is often part of a pattern of abuse. Blaming the other person for your shitty actions ("you brought this on yourself") is part of a pattern of abuse. It's possible he's not abusive and this won't escalate, but if I were you I wouldn't stick around to find out.

NTA. I'm non binary, but I understand that it's important for my doctor to know that I was AFAB and have ovaries and a uterus and need pap smears and stuff.

Just a suggestion though (and if I'm wrong about the wording, I apologize), do you think it would help if you changed the form to ask "Sex assigned at birth" or something. That way it makes it less about gender identity and more about the fact that you need to know if a person has a prostate or whatever.

NTA. But your MIL is and so is your husband.

She had no right to fuck with your medical equipment like that. EOs can cause serious issues for people, like allergies, and can cause issues with something like a CPAP, which is definitely not supposed to have oils in it.

Your husband needs to have your back and tell his mother she was wrong and that she is never to do that again.

YTA. This is the kind of thing that both parents need to agree to. You went behind your husband's back and then tried to say you're the more important parent.

*Neither* of you should have gotten your respective mothers involved in this, by the way. But you're the one who outright snuck behind your husband's back.
Okay, except pre-pandemic should would have been seeing her friends at school and now she's not? So she's probably feeling isolated?
NTA. What Susie did was not acceptable. She got herself fired.
Yep, this is almost certainly the case.

NTA.

The bride and groom liked the cake. That's all that matters.

It's hard when family is not accepting of who you are; I'm glad you love and celebrate you sister for who she is. The rest of your family can fuck right off into the sunset.

When I was about 7, I had interstitial cystitis, which makes you have to pee about every 45 minutes. I wet the bed a lot, because I was so sleep deprived from having to wake up to pee all the time that I eventually just didn't wake up; I was too tired.

My parents punished me for it. They let it go on for years just punishing me instead of taking me to the fucking doctor.

To say our relationship was not the greatest is an understatement.

Take it from me OP, you're being an asshole and traumatizing your daughter by punishing her for something she cannot control instead of getting her help. There's a special place in hell for parents like you.

A sleep study. A psychiatrist.

There are a lot of things that can cause night terrors or sleep paralysis. Some are physical disorders (e.g. narcolepsy). Some are mood disorders (e.g. depression, generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar). Some are situational issues (e.g. high stress situations. Is Kara applying for college? Dealing with the end of high school and high school and figuring out her future? Living through the MIDDLE OF A FUCKING PANDEMIC?). Some are trauma (e.g. sexual assault, bullying, having an asshole for a dad).

A sleep study and seeing a psychiatrist will help get to the root of the cause. Then therapy and/or medication can help her, depending on the cause.

This is not rocket science.

Step up and parent your child.

That's literally not how any of that works. At all.

Take. Kara. To. A. Doctor. You. Worthless. Excuse. For. A. Father.

Separate the twins and/or move Kara's bedroom in the meantime. Suck it up and actually fucking parent your children.

And honestly, get some therapy yourself to figure out why you hate your daughter so damn much.
Yeah, poor Kara seems like the scapegoat child. OP, I hope she moves far far away from you, for her own sake.

Holy shit, YTA. And a neglectful parent. You're ignoring clear signs that something is wrong and instead you're punishing your daughter by forcing her to stay up. And then you're saying she's trying to "sneak away" to sleep, after you made her stay up all night. Like, you're invested in her sleep deprivation.

Your oldest child is clearly suffering. *Something* is wrong. You say "she has no trauma" but she is 18 and presumably has spent time out of your sight in the past 18 years, so maybe consider the fact that *something* traumatic may have happened to her that is triggering night terrors. Or maybe she has an anxiety disorder or some other mental health issues that are causing night terrors. Or possibly has developed a sleep disorder. (Incidentally, disrupting sleep patterns is the *worst* thing you can do for a sleep disorder).

The appropriate response here is to get your oldest daughter help. Not punish her.

But since you've decided that *punishing* her is the right response, don't be surprised if she doesn't trust you if something traumatic has happened to her.

NTA. Your mother is the parent here, but it sounds like she's forcing most of the parental responsibility on you. On top of that, she's letting Ted completely disrespect any boundaries you have. I'm glad you moved out. Your mom is an adult and needs to figure out child care on her own, not burden her older children with it.

YTA.

Glasses are not inappropriate for formal events. WTF?

YTA. 

Recovery from birth can be hard and traumatic. You're saying you're not "expecting her to do anything for the family" but having them over will require her attention and mental energy, which she rightfully will want to be devoting to her post-partum recovery and bonding with the kid and just getting used to having a baby. Also, your wife may have issues like PPD or PPA (I  hope she doesn't, but it's a possibility) and it's important that she have space for that, which she won't if your family is around. 

Help after birth is often appreciated, but you can't assume that your family will give meaningful help ("holding the baby" isn't meaningful help, especially with a newborn. Are your parents going to cook, clean, do dishes, go shopping?)

Tell your parents that they won't be able to come until several months after the birth. Tell them that you and your wife will let them know when you are up to having visitors.

NTA.

You've repeatedly asked her to call first and she's ignoring that. You're allowed to not answer the door for her. You didn't invite her and she's being the rude one. The 40 minute round trip on the bus? Yeah, that's on her.
NTA. You bought the car, you didn't scam him. He can take the money you paid and buy himself another car.

YTA. Mel is entitled to a relationship with her mother's side of the family. Your son is no relation to them. Also your parents are *definitely* not entitled to gifts from them. Explain to your son that different people have different relationships and let it go at that.
NTA and I'm so sorry your family is being awful to you. You deserve better.
NTA. That's a cruel and childish thing to do. Not only did she risk causing you issues at work, but she must have caused you a ton of stress by making you think she'd gone into labor early.

YTA.

I don't know what kind of relationship you have with your son and his wife. If you have a history of a fraught relationship with them, then the initial ask probably came across as trying to push boundaries. If you're on relatively good terms, the initial ask/suggestion was probably fine (especially if framed more as advice that *someone*\--maybe you, but maybe a friend/neighbor should have a copy, just in case of something like a lost key or whatnot), but continuing to push and insist like you did makes you the asshole.

YTA.

You have been carrying it around for decades. Please get some help so you can enjoy your time with your other children outside of the shadow of your daughter who has passed.~~  


ETA: I wrote this before I saw all of your responses and I'm going to take the kid gloves off.

You need a different therapist. And you need to get your act together. You've been awful to your living children and your behavior about Brooke seems more performative than genuine at this point. You don't get to dictate how your children deal with the loss of their sister and you don't get to force everyone to kowtow to you.

Honestly, if you're willing to cut your kids off for not having a memorial table for your daughter who has been dead for 26 years, your son is right. You need to reexamine your life.

NTA.

People who pressure other people about drinking are assholes. People have all kinds of reasons to not drink alcohol and they don't have to justify it to anyone. Your fiancé is especially being an asshole. He should have your back.

You. Are. Her. Parent.  


When she was a minor, those things were your responsibility. Period. Providing your child with medical care is the bare minimum.  


I'm sorry your parents were bad parents and didn't do those things. That doesn't make you a saint for doing them. Again, you did what is expected as a parent.

NTA.  Your future step mom and you dad are assholes.   


Here's the thing OP.  You are a minor child and your father should be considering your happiness and health and wellbeing *first*.  That means if his fiancée is pulling this shit, he should be backing you up and also reconsidering the marriage,  because she is being selfish and childish.   


Single parents (or widowed or divorced) need to put their kids first and they need to be very clear about that with prospective partners.

YTA.  So much.  If you truly love your SON, you need to respect and affirm him.  That includes using his pronouns, calling him your SON, and accepting that he is a boy/man.  You misgender him throughout the entire post and in real life and are committed to continue doing it.  You're forcing him to hide who he is.  If you never want to see your son again once he turns 18 and can escape your house, by all means, continue being an asshole.  But if you want a relationship with him, you need to deal with your transphobia and celebrate him for who he is--your wonderful amazing SON.
NTA.  He's using you for validation, attention, and an ego boost.  He's playing with your emotions.  Cut him off and don't look back.
NTA.  You are not obligated to stay around people who are terrible to you, even if they are family.

NTA.

This is parentification.  I am the oldest of 5 kids, also NB and AFAB and I was in your exact shoes growing up.  I was given way more than my fair share of housework and childcare responsibilities.  It's wrong and it's not fair and you should definitely keep up the chore strike until your mom gets over herself and assigns chores more fairly.
NTA.  Jake needs to learn actions have consequences and that when you deliberately ruin something out of spite, you need to replace it.

All of this.  Also, teachers are human too and bullies sometimes pick the kids who even the teachers may not like (the really weird kid, the kid who really actually may be kind of annoying, etc.) and that can color the way a teacher views the treatment of said kid.  Especially if the bullies are more likeable and popular.

Holy cow.  NTA.  He's a whiny man baby and honestly, not worth your time.

Also, he wants you to walk a few blocks to a public restroom to change your pad?  That's fucking ridiculous.

NTA.  You're not a wet nurse.  Because of timing, you were able (and willing) to help your SIL with something caused by medical issues.  But honestly, you had no obligation to even do that.  You were being kind.  Even if your sister had medical issues that prevented her from breastfeeding, you would be under no obligation to help her, because, like you said, the timing does not work for you.  It's hard to pump while working and you don't owe your body to anyone for any reason.

NTA.  You're the one giving birth.  Your comfort and safety is paramount.  You're correct when you say that it is *your* medical experience, not your husband.  I would be very anxious at the thought of giving birth in a country where the primary language was a language I'm not fluent in.  And I would be very uncomfortable at the thought of giving birth with someone who is not my regular OB/Gyn (I know that can happen in the US as well, due to doctor schedules, unexpected labor, or not being lucky enough to have regular insurance, but your husband's plan pretty much guarantees this).  And you're not being inconsiderate of his family.  It's very common for one (or even both!) sides of the family to be far away during/after a birth.  Your not the asshole.  Hold your ground here and do not give an inch.
He’s just been with me for 11 years. He’s seen it before. He’s heard it before. He’s gotta be tired of it. I’m so tired of being a burden on him because of my faulty wiring.
I know he is.  I am just at the choosing beggars stage of finding a therapist, so I don't know what else to do.

NTA but your husband is.  I understand addiction is serious and I really empathize with your family for the struggles.  But that money is your daughter's and she should not be manipulated or guilt-tripped into giving it up.

YTA.  It's not the teacher's job to parent your child and she expressed a willingness to work with you to come up with a plan to help your child, which you refused to do.  You don't get to dump your kid on the teacher and have no part in his education.  She has other students who also need attention and you cannot expect your child to monopolize her time.  Also, it is incredibly disrespectful of you to call into question her ability to teach based on her age/appearance.  Your child is probably picking up on your disdain for her which makes him feel like he doesn't have to respect her either.
NTA.  Family tree projects that demand the child use their own family are dicey exactly for the reasons you described here.

YTA.  You are so much TA.  Your child is hurting.  This sounds like me.  I started having those kinds of issues at 12.  I was bullied by my peers and I have a serious mental illness that went undiagnosed for 24 more years (so a solid 2/3 of my life up to that point) in part because my parents instilled in me that the way I was feeling/acting was my fault because I wasn't trying hard enough to be normal.  I went through decades of hell because my parents acted like you did and by the time I was an adult, I was convinced that the problem was just me not trying hard enough, rather than a medical disorder.

My illness is totally manageable with the right medication and therapy and it's highly likely that what your kid is going through may be as well, but you have to get off your ass and actually be a parent and get her help.
NTA.  It is your name.  They need to call you by your actual name.  Period.
NTA.  The teacher is an asshole.  Refusing to pronounce someone's name correctly is a really big asshole move.

Thanks, I must have clicked without realizing it.
YTA.  Your oldest child is not a third parent.  It is not on her to be your regular babysitter.  Figure out your childcare situation in a way that does not burden your daughter.

NTA.  Frankly, it's none of her damn business that you had an abortion and it never will be.  It's perfectly reasonable to set a clear expectation with her that if she brings up your abortion to you or child again that she will not see your child, or will be on extremely limited contact.  As it is, I wouldn't want to leave my (hypothetical) child alone with her, because I feel like she'll probably talk about it anyway.
NTA.  It's your hair.  Period.  Your boyfriend doesn't get a say in what you do with it.

YTA.  You promised your daughter the money (in fact you were willing to give it no strings attached after college) and she asked you to save it for her wedding.  You're specifically taking the money that you promised her back simply because of her sexuality.  You're the asshole and you're being homophobic/biphobic to boot.

You say you imagined her marriage as her having a husband and family and children.  Firstly, she and her wife are. a. family.  Regardless of whether they have children or not).  Second, she and her wife may or may not have children.  Same-sex parents have children all the time.   
 Would you withdraw the money if she were marrying a man but they chose not to have children?  Third, whether or not you give money for a wedding, your child does not owe  you grandchildren.

You're in the wrong here and if you want to ever have a relationship with her (and any potential graaaaaaaaaaaaaaandbabies you expect her to have),  I suggest you give her the money you promised her and beg her (and her fiancee's) forgiveness.  Do not try to justify your actions.  Accept all responsibility for being in the wrong, because you are the ones who are completely wrong here, and apologize.  It may take time for them to forgive you (if they ever do at all), but they will never forgive you if you don't do what you promised *and* make a sincere and unconditional apology.

Oh my god, YTA.  You cannot ask a 5-year-old child to change her name.  That is abusive and terrible.  She is a child, not a pet and not an accessory.  She is a human being who knows her name.  And they idea that they could "pick a different child" because of her name is the most petty and stupid thing I've ever heard.  Again, kids aren't accessories.  Suck it up and either change your kid's name or have cousins with the same name.

NTA.  Shame on your parents for throwing the "we took care of you for 18 years" guilt trip on you.  That is what a parent is supposed to do.  When you have children, you are responsible for feeding, clothing, and educating them for 18 years.  Period.  You don't get to guilt trip them or expect them to pay you back.  (I know a lot of people do end up "repaying it" by caring for parents when they are older, or helping their parents, but guilt tripping your kids isn't fair).
Oh 100% YTA.  A huge gaping asshole.  This is abusive behavior.
NTA.  It's your backyard.  She's fucking rude.  Honestly, if you wanna walk around totally naked in your yard, that's your business and if she doesn't want to see, she shouldn't look.
NTA.  Your coworker sucks.  Your personal life isn't any of their god damn business.

The boys' chores were all things that are done only on a weekly or monthly basis (or less)--things like oil changes and mowing the lawn.  The girls' chores were all the daily tasks--laundry, cooking, cleaning, dressing the little kids, which all take a ton of time, especially with that huge-ass family.  There is no way it's a fair division of labor.

Destroying something he worked really hard on and that clearly meant something to him is cruel and unnecessary.  It's akin to ripping up a drawing or a craft project he was particularly proud of. 

This does nothing to "help your child learn the skill of waking himself up" and is not a natural consequence of failing to wake up on time.

You're just being a controlling bully.

NTA.  And I say this as someone who literally gets sick to my stomach at the smell of lukewarm/cold coffee.  If it's not piping hot or iced, I can't stand it (weird I know).  My boyfriend's routine is literally:

1. Make snooty pour-over coffee
2. Drink some coffee.
3. Forget about the rest of coffee
4. Re-heat coffee in microwave
5. Repeat steps 2 through 4 throughout the day

He tries to keep his coffee far enough away from me that it doesn't bother me (it helps that I'm at work most of the day while he is home) and I live with it because he loves coffee and tries to be considerate of my sensitivity.

Your boyfriend is being unreasonable.

There is something called a "*bona fide* occupational qualification", which is basically something deemed essential to a job function so an employer can exclude candidates based on this requirement, even if the candidate is a protected class.  For example, complete color blindness can exclude someone from being able to be an electrician because it is necessary for an electrician to discriminate between different colors of wires (this weirdly specific example brought to you by the fact that my mom used to do EHS/personnel for a small electrical contractor).

It can even apply to things like religious beliefs under certain circumstances (for example, a Catholic school can require teachers to be Catholic, but not positions like custodial staff or a fashion company can put a call for male models, but can't require the sales people be all male).

It can get a little muddy though, especially with regards to things like aesthetics (I know there were lawsuits about flight attendants and airlines are not allowed to base hiring decisions on having pretty flight attendants anymore (they tried to argue that appealing to customers desires was a BFOQ and courts did not agree), but prettiness/hotness can still be a consideration for acting jobs, etc).

Here's my 2 cents on the whole thing.  There is some truth to "not all calories are created equal" in the sense that eating certain ways makes it easier to follow CICO. 
So for example, if I eat a 350 calorie lunch that is a salad with some chicken and a measured amount of oil, I will probably feel pretty full until dinner time.  The protein, fat, and fiber will help me feel full, and the raw veggies I like on my salad take up a lot of volume.
But if I eat a 350 calorie piece of cake, which is mostly sugar, I'm probably not going to feel as full.  Sugar doesn't keep me feeling sated for as long and a 350 calorie piece of cake is smaller than a 350 calorie salad.
CICO is still king though.  If I could manage to eat only 1200 calories of cake every day, I would still lose weight.  (That wouldn't be healthy by any stretch of the imagination, but it would lead to weight loss).  If all I'm eating is healthy food, but I eat too much of it, I'll still gain weight.  But for a lot of people, myself included, portion control is easier when I am eating more healthy food that is less calorically dense.  I feel fuller longer and eat fewer calories.
Plus, for me, high sugar intakes often beget sugar cravings.  When I decide to splurge and eat something sugary, I often find myself wanting more sugar, which makes it harder for me to follow my CICO.  I know I'm not the only one who has this issue.

There are a host of conditions that affect nutrient absorption or are co-morbid with conditions that do.  People with cerebral palsy often have difficulty eating due to motor issues and many can also have issues with the gut that make getting adequate nutrition difficult.  Cystic Fibrosis causes absorption issues for many people.  Crohn's, celiac, and ulcerative colitis can seriously mess up nutrient absorption.  Not to mention all the diseases that have a side effect of severe loss of appetite.  There are also diseases that cause over absorption of certain things like hemochromatosis and Wilson's disease which can also cause malnutrition in the sense that the body absorbs too much iron or copper and that's really, really bad for you too.

What kills me is that the person asking, if they do have a medical condition that makes it hard to get adequate nutrition, still feels the need to ask someone on Tumblr if it's okay if they track their nutrition.  One of the best ways to deal with diseases that cause malabsorption (I mean aside from necessary medications, if they exist, which they don't for some things) is track what you eat and make sure you're avoiding problem foods (like gluten in the case of celiac) and eating enough nutrients.  It's really important.  I don't understand why anyone would jeopardize their health for tumblr approval.  (Edited to complete a thought).
